prompt: A quilt block is built from equilateral triangles — every side of each triangle is the same length. What is the measure of each angle in one of those triangles?
hint: Equal sides force equal angles, so all three angles are the same size.

hints.text: Equal sides force equal angles, so all three angles are the same size.
Three equal angles must share $180^\circ$ evenly.

explanation: An equilateral triangle has three congruent sides, so it is also equiangular — all three angles are equal.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why quilters love them
steps: Six equilateral triangles fit around a single point with no gaps, because $6 \times 60 = 360^\circ$ — a full turn.
That is exactly why a $60^\circ$ corner tiles so cleanly into hexagon quilt blocks.
